drivingQuestion: Why is covering the blood required only once, when returning a lost item is required even a hundred times?
outcomeNote: Rav Ashi's distinction stands unchallenged; the difficulty raised in the previous unit is answered.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם לָא כְּתִיב מִיעוּטָא, הָכָא כְּתִיב מִיעוּטָא ״וְכִסָּהוּ״.
segments.en: Rav Ashi «said to» Rav Aḥa: «There,» in the verse discussing the obligation to return a lost item, «a restriction is not written» in the verse to limit the obligation. «Here,» in the verse discussing the obligation to cover the blood, «a restriction is written,» as the verse states: «“And he shall cover it.”» The usage of the term “it” indicates that one must cover the blood only one time.

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: התם לא כתיב מיעוטא
moves.summary: Rav Ashi answers that no restrictive term is written regarding a lost item.
moves.about: answering that no restrictive term is written for returning a lost item, whereas the covering verse writes one

moves.summary: Here the verse writes וכסהו, a restriction confining the duty to one act of covering.
moves.about: citing and he shall cover it as the restrictive term limiting the covering obligation
